measure.label: Dropback
measure.text: A pass attempt or a sack. A scramble is a run and is not counted.

measure.label: EPA per dropback
measure.text: Expected points added per dropback, on the model every Stats page uses.

measure.label: Success rate
measure.text: Share of dropbacks that gained 50% of the distance on 1st down, 70% on 2nd, or 100% on 3rd and 4th down.

measure.label: Garbage time
measure.text: Plays in a blowout's final stretch are left out of dropbacks, EPA and success rate. The attempts, yards, touchdowns, interceptions and sacks columns are full-season totals.

measure.label: Pool
measure.text: Games between two of the 18 programs, the only games with play-by-play.

questions.question: Why does a team that rarely goes three-and-out still rank near the bottom on offense?
questions.why_asked: Top third in fewest three-and-outs, and bottom third in adjusted offense or top third in empty drives dying in their own territory.
questions.answer: PVAMU rarely go three-and-out (10 of 60 drives), yet 21 of their 33 empty drives still died in their own territory, 8 of them after a first down; most never got one. Once past midfield they are about average: 23 of 38 trips scored. The offense's problem is getting to midfield.

claims.text: Three-and-outs: 10 of 60 drives (16.7%, 2nd of 13, fewest first).
Offense, opponent-adjusted EPA per play: -0.102 (12th of 13; league -0.011)
33 of 60 drives scored nothing; 21 of those ended in their own territory, and 8 of those 21 had picked up at least one first down first.
Once past midfield: 23 of 38 drives scored, 3.71 points per trip (7th of 13).
Second-down success: 43% (league 40%), 8.4 yards to go on average.
Third-down success: 33% (league 38%), 8.0 yards to go on average.

questions.question: How are they leading the division with these numbers?
questions.why_asked: First in the standings, bottom third in opponent-adjusted EPA on one side of the ball.
questions.answer: The standings and the play-by-play disagree: PVAMU lead the division while ranking 12th of 13 in adjusted offense. Their largest edge on the field is where drives start (2nd of 13).

claims.text: PVAMU lead the SWAC West at 3-2 in conference play (3-1 in the division), 43.3% to win it.
Offense, opponent-adjusted EPA per play: -0.102 (12th of 13; league -0.011)
One-score conference games: 2-1.
Average drive start: own 36 (2nd of 13; league own 31)

questions.question: What decides their games?
questions.why_asked: Every team: the battles that separate its wins from its losses.
questions.answer: PVAMU won the success rate and average drive start battles in all but one of their 5 games with play-by-play.

claims.text: What decides their games in their 5 games with play-by-play: turnovers (fewer) 1-0 when won, 0-2 when lost; havoc rate 3-0 when won, 0-2 when lost; penalties (fewer) 3-0 when won, 0-2 when lost.
League-wide since 2019, the team that wins the turnovers (fewer) battle wins 76% of games (69% of one-score games, 342 games).
League-wide since 2019, the team that wins the havoc rate battle wins 71% of games (61% of one-score games, 440 games).
Loss to MVSU: lost yards per drive (18.4 to 25.7), yards per play (4.0 to 5.5), epa per play (-0.18 to +0.08), sack battle (0 to 4).

questions.question: How much does field position carry them?
questions.why_asked: Top third in average drive start, or in where opponents start.
questions.answer: PVAMU start drives at own 36, 2nd of 13. Field position is one of their strongest edges, and much of it comes from special teams.

claims.text: Average drive start: own 36 (2nd of 13; league own 31)
Defense: opponents' average start: own 26 (2nd of 13; league own 32)
Net field position: +10.2 yards per drive (Team Analytics).
Special-teams attributes earned: Field Flippers, Lockdown Coverage (provisional: 5 of 6 games).
Points per drive rank 6th, adjusted EPA rank 12th: the short field is worth more than the snaps.

questions.question: Is the turnover battle costing them?
questions.why_asked: Bottom third in turnover margin, or in takeaways per drive.
questions.answer: PVAMU lose the turnover battle: -0.60 a game. The giveaways and the lack of takeaways both count.

claims.text: Turnover margin per game: -0.60 (12th of 13; league 0.00)
Own drives ending in a turnover: 7 of 60.
Opponent drives ending in a takeaway: 4 of 58 (13th of 13, most first).

questions.question: Why does a defense that keeps teams off the board break in the red zone?
questions.why_asked: Top third in opponent scoring rate, bottom third in red-zone touchdowns allowed.
questions.answer: The defense keeps most drives off the board, but once an opponent reaches the 20 it usually scores a touchdown.

claims.text: Opponent drives that score: 29% (2nd of 13, fewest first).
Defense: red-zone TD rate allowed: 80% (12th of 13; league 68%), on 20 opponent trips.

questions.question: Why do they fade late?
questions.why_asked: Bottom third in 4th-quarter margin without a slow start.
questions.answer: PVAMU win the early quarters and give it back late.

claims.text: Margin per game by quarter: Q1 6.80 (2nd of 13), Q2 -0.80 (11th of 13), Q3 4.20 (4th of 13), Q4 -3.60 (12th of 13).
Week 5: led MVSU by 24 and lost 27-28.

questions.question: What changed from last season?
questions.why_asked: Top third of the league in how far adjusted EPA moved from last season (40+ percentile points, offense + defense).
questions.answer: 14 metrics fell 25 percentile points or more and 1 rose that much; adjusted EPA moved 118 percentile points across offense and defense (4th of 13 in the league).

claims.text: 2025: 10-4 (7-1 in conference), division finish 1.
Worse: Defense: red-zone TD rate allowed: 58% (6th of 18) to 80% (12th of 13).
Worse: Defense: adjusted EPA/play allowed: -0.071 (2nd of 18) to -0.012 (9th of 13).
Worse: Sack rate allowed: 1% (1st of 18) to 7% (8th of 13).
Worse: Opponent-adjusted EPA/play: +0.094 (7th of 18) to -0.102 (12th of 13).
Worse: 3rd/4th-down success: 47% (5th of 18) to 35% (10th of 13).
Better: Defense: opponents' average start: own 30 (9th of 18) to own 26 (2nd of 13).

questions.question: Do they win the three-and-out battle?
questions.why_asked: Top or bottom two on the three-and-out board, either side.
questions.answer: The three-and-out battle is one of their edges.

claims.text: Offense went three-and-out on 10 of 60 drives (16.7%, 2nd of 13).

three_and_outs.definition: A three-and-out is a drive of three official plays or fewer (runs, passes and sacks that stood) that ends in a punt. Rate = three-and-outs / drives. Kneel-only possessions are not drives.

third_and_long.definition: 3rd and 7 or more to go. Converted = the offense kept the ball with a new set of downs or scored a touchdown (a penalty first down counts). Plays wiped by a penalty are not attempts.
